pull.title: KAFKA-21253: Always clear record collector offsets in closeDirty
pull.body:
`RecordCollectorImpl.closeDirty()` aborts the open transaction before
calling `close()`, which clears the collector's changelog offsets. If
the abort throws, `close()` is skipped and the offsets are kept. This
happens with an `IllegalStateException` after a timed-out
`commitTransaction()`. The revived task reuses the collector, so if it
is closed clean while its wiped store is still restoring, those stale
offsets are checkpointed. The next restore then skips the missing
records.

This change moves `close()` into a `finally` block so the offsets are
always cleared. It also logs the abort failure at ERROR before
rethrowing. The caller still swallows the exception, and before this
change it was only logged at DEBUG, without the exception.

`CommitTimeoutDirtyCloseIntegrationTest` uses the fault proxy to
reproduce this. A delayed EndTxn leaves a commit pending, so the abort
fails. A later `ILLEGAL_GENERATION` on `TxnOffsetCommit` migrates the
thread, and the restoring task is closed clean.

The associated integration test replicates the issue and without the fix
in this PR it fails.

Reviewers: Lucas Brutschy <lbrutschy@confluent.io>

### 🟡 Changes recommended The ERROR log omits its exception, and the cleanup path can mask the original abort failure.
1 open finding - [Include exception details in commit/abort failure log](https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23791#discussion_r4269258924) · New
1 resolved since last review - [Ensure corrupted task returns to instance A before marker query](https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23791#discussion_r4256391389)
Previously missed (1) In code that hasn't changed since last review
Preserve abort exception when close throws in finally `streams/​src/​main/​java/​org/​apache/​kafka/​streams/​processor/​internals/​RecordCollectorImpl.java:612` Calling `close()` from `finally` can replace the abort failure with a different exception: `close()` invokes `checkForException()`, which throws any pending asynchronous producer error, and an exception thrown by a `finally` block masks the original one. Clear the offsets in `finally`, but run `checkForException()` only after a successful abort, preserving the previous exception semantics while ensuring offsets are always removed.
🧠 **Review effort:** Balanced

review_comments.body: `ILLEGAL_GENERATION` sends the stream thread through `handleTaskMigrated`, which unsubscribes and rejoins the group (`StreamThread.java:1182-1189`). The rebalance is not guaranteed to return `corruptedTask` to instance A; with zero standbys, querying A for the marker can therefore time out even when the fix works, and another owner would not exercise A's stale checkpoint. Force this task back onto instance A (for example, make B leave the group and wait until `activeTasks(instanceA)` contains it) before producing and querying the marker.

`close()` ends with `checkForException()`, so if there is a pending send error it will be thrown from this `finally` and replace the abort exception. Previously the abort failure was what the caller saw. Is that intended? If not, maybe clear the offsets in the `finally` and only call `checkForException()` on the normal path (or `addSuppressed`).

Do we need the catch just for logging? The caller already catches and logs this, so we'd get the failure logged twice, and `Throwable` also covers errors like OOM. Could this just be try/finally, with the log level raised in the caller?
Unrelated to this change, but `closeClean()` calls `removeAllProducedSensors()` and `closeDirty()` doesn't. Is that on purpose?

These client ids (`-StateUpdater-1-restore-consumer`, `-StreamThread-1-producer`) depend on internal thread naming. If that changes, the fault rules silently don't match and the test only fails after the 120s wait. Can we derive them from the thread metadata instead?

This depends a lot on timing (2s max.block.ms, 6s EndTxn delay, `once()` rules). On a loaded CI machine the delayed EndTxn could hit a different transaction, or the restore could finish before the ILLEGAL_GENERATION fires. Since new tests get run 20x for deflaking, have you run it repeatedly under load?

This sums every metric named `txn-commit-time-ns-total` regardless of group/tags and casts `metricValue()` to double. Could it throw a ClassCastException or go down when a thread's metrics are removed in a rebalance? Maybe filter on the thread-level group and tags.

Would a small unit test in `RecordCollectorTest` be worth adding too (producer whose `abortTransaction()` throws, then assert `offsets()` is empty)? It would be a deterministic guard for the fix, the integration test is slow and timing dependent.
Nit: the class qualifier on `NUM_KEYS` is redundant. Also `produce()` creates a new producer on every call. `IntegrationTestUtils.produceKeyValuesSynchronously` might do the same job.

I agree with just having the `try/finally` but we never see an error from the abort exception `close()` executes `TaskManager.executeAndMaybeSwallow` for `recordCollector.closeDirty()` which catches the exception and issues a debug log statement.  Thinking about this more I don't agree with this and I'll make the log statement there an `ERROR`.
answered above
That I don't know, I'll look into this in a follow-up PR

`ThreadMetadata.restoreConsumerClientId()` returns `instance-a-StreamThread-1-restore-consumer` but it's actually created in the `StateUpdater` as  `instance-a-StateUpdater-1-restore-consumer` I'll do a follow-up PR to fix this and clean up here after that. Does that work for you?

`produceKeyValuesSynchronously` can't target a partition, and the partition-aware `produceSynchronously` still opens a producer per call, so I kept the local helper but now create the producer once in setUp and close it in tearDown.

Yes I ran it 20x under load, all 20/20 passed.
 In every run the `EndTxn` delay hit the intended commit, and the restore was 
 suspended roughly at 15–27 of 303 records.
I've added a filter for the producer client.id

Instance-a gets the task back because the HA assignor moves it to the most caught-up client, and instance-b has no local state for it. That depends on instance-a having restored at least one batch before handleLostAll(), so the test now waits for the first restored batch before triggering the ILLEGAL_GENERATION. Reran 20x under load: the task came back to instance-a every time.

The lambda drops `e`, so this logs only the name and neither the message nor the stack trace. Should it be `log.error("Error closing unclean {}", name, e)`? Also, this covers every dirty close, not just the abort failure, so I wonder if ERROR gets noisy for expected errors.

Coming back to my earlier question: `close()` still calls `checkForException()`, so a pending send error thrown here replaces the abort exception. Is that fine, or should the offsets be cleared in the `finally` and the send error thrown only on the normal path?
Nit: whitespace-only line.

The exception is still omitted from this ERROR log, so the timed-out commit/abort failure is reported without its type, message, or stack trace. Pass `e` as the trailing SLF4J argument so the new log provides the diagnostic information described by the change.

yeah I get that but leaving at debug is not great either, we spent a lot of time tracking down the current issue because there was nothing in the logs. I've put at at `WARN` which follows the general pattern in `TaskManager`
yeah I agree - sorry I missed that before
